headline: Highest risk is medium: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots/clipboard while EMQX exposes broad HTTP/network surfaces, creating plausible leakage and workflow-conflict paths; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported app content, while EMQX exposes HTTP API and broad network egress. That creates a plausible manual or file-based injection bridge, but no shared channel or direct parser-to-parser path is documented, so the blast radius is limited and uncertainty keeps this low rather than none.
conditions: IF the operator copies EMQX-controlled text into ChatGPT Desktop or opens EMQX-derived files in ChatGPT Desktop
IF EMQX output is pasted into a prompt or screenshot that ChatGPT Desktop reads
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Use a human review step before pasting EMQX output into ChatGPT Desktop
Strip instructions from EMQX-generated text before reuse
Keep EMQX outputs in a separate workspace from ChatGPT inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while EMQX handles IoT data and has broad network egress. If data from ChatGPT Desktop is forwarded into EMQX workflows, sensitive content can leave the local context. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF uploaded files, screenshots, or IDE code from ChatGPT Desktop are forwarded into EMQX-connected systems
IF EMQX publishes or relays payloads that include content originating from ChatGPT Desktop
mitigations: Avoid sending ChatGPT Desktop artifacts into EMQX topics or APIs
Redact secrets from files before any transfer
Use separate accounts or principals for the two systems
Log and review outbound EMQX payloads for sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read filesystem content and supported app files, and EMQX can accept HTTP API traffic with broad egress. Even without write access from ChatGPT Desktop, both can act on overlapping data flows and external endpoints, so coordination failures are plausible. Because write conflict is not present, this stays medium.
conditions: IF the operator uses EMQX HTTP APIs to mutate shared state derived from ChatGPT Desktop outputs
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads files that EMQX also updates through external systems
mitigations: Assign one system as read-only for shared artifacts
Introduce a manual lock or ticket before mutating shared resources
Separate EMQX test topics from production topics
Keep ChatGPT Desktop away from files that EMQX writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce analysis from files and app context, and EMQX can consume HTTP API inputs and relay IoT data. If EMQX treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or routing. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF EMQX ingests ChatGPT Desktop output without validation
IF ChatGPT Desktop-generated recommendations are used to drive EMQX routing or automation
mitigations: Require a human check before EMQX consumes ChatGPT output
Add schema validation to all ChatGPT-derived payloads
Tag AI-generated fields and exclude them from automation rules
Use a staging topic or queue for first-pass review

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop is documented as touching uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while EMQX is documented only as handling IoT data. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is stated in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to a documented gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are placed into ChatGPT Desktop and then forwarded into EMQX-managed flows
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not stated in either profile
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either system
Keep regulated data out of ChatGPT Desktop workflows
Document retention and residency assumptions for EMQX
Review vendor terms before using sensitive datasets
